fullText:
a16z's Connor Love on why the old defense model gave soldiers systems "developed for 10 years ago," and how private capital lets startups build what they need before the Pentagon asks:

"I experienced this in my past when I served in the Army. The buyer is not the user, and the appropriator of the dollars for the buyer is completely removed."

"You had primes who would just sit there and listen, like, 'Tell me what you want. I'll develop the thing after you give me the money.'... You get a system that was developed for 10 years ago."

"The beautiful thing is venture capital and what we do in American Dynamism, but also the rest of the capital markets is saying, 'We will actually fund that in advance.'"

"The outcome of that is the soldier gets a better product, gets something that actually fundamentally changes the battlefield and helps with deterrence or security or safety."

"More importantly, you get a type of system that is actually aligned with the requirement of the market and what technology can do today."

"Instead of sitting and waiting for the government to tell you what they want, the government signals, and you see it, and you build it in advance by using private capital, and that just has not happened in the history of defense."

@ConnorLoveCA

fullText:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash, on more of your hardware.

Quantizing a 428B model opens up more ways to run it locally. Lower-bit weights reduce the memory needed to load the model and the weight data moved during decoding. Making those savings useful takes careful calibration, efficient low-bit kernels, and hardware-aware placement of experts across GPU and system RAM.

Thank you to the builders doing that work:

• @UnslothAI @danielhanchen — 2-bit Dynamic GGUF weights at 143.9 GB, with calibration and fidelity testing across coding, tool use and other workloads.
• @ViC305 — SAGE-EXL3, token-level fidelity measurements and a single-DGX-Spark recipe.
• @PeasantSmith — Project Maya quants and expert offloading for local coding and tool use.
• @MiaAI_lab — EXL3-EAQ quantization work.
• @jundotkim + mlx-community — oQ quants and DSpark-powered decoding through oMLX on Apple Silicon.
• @AIatAMD — Quark MXFP4 adapted for AMD Instinct.
• @atomic_chat_hq — GGUFs for local desktop workflows.
• @superalesha — custom inference work combining quantized weights, expert caching and system RAM on 4× RTX 3090.
Every shared quant, kernel, measurement and recipe gives the next builder a better starting point. Thank you.

For people working on ChatGPT at OpenAI, here are some fun puzzle games you might enjoy:

- There are 4 places to set up browser access for ChatGPT app. Can you find them all?

-  There are 3 places to store passwords in ChatGPT app. Can you find them all? Bonus: if you can also tell which part of app uses which passwords.

- How many different modes are in ChatGPT? Hint: It's more than just Chat, Work, Codex.

- Projects for each mode in ChatGPT is different in their own mysterious ways. Can you list all the differences?

- If your user eventually had created 100+ projects, list all the ways things will be unusable.

- Your user frequently moves between desktop, laptop and phone. Draw a full 3 dimensional tensor of modes, device and capabilities.

Good luck!
